stories.title: The U.S. women's hockey team is dominating the Olympics. Now they will play for gold
stories.summary: The Americans, whose captain Hilary Knight is leading a generation of thrilling young talent, are undefeated through six games at the Olympics — and they're outscoring their opponents 31 to 1.

stories.title: Extremist rhetoric is often found in government messaging. Who's the target?
stories.summary: In a rare move, the White House took down a racist post last week from one of President Trump's social media accounts. But extremism researchers say it fits a pattern of mainstreaming extremist ideas.

stories.title: On the streets of Beijing, many wish for economic stability this Lunar New Year
stories.summary: It's the Year of the Fire Horse. In the Chinese zodiac, the fire horse represents action and risk-taking. But on the streets of Beijing, many say they just want stability in this sluggish economy.

stories.title: Ramadan in Cairo blends the old and the new
stories.summary: The world's Muslims are preparing for the holy month of Ramadan, a time of fasting and prayer. In Cairo, that means shopping for gifts and buying decorations to get into the spirit of the holy month.

stories.title: Part comedy, part masochism: This stand-up show includes a public roast of each comic
stories.summary: Every Sunday in Austin, there's a comedy show called Banana Phone. Comedians do one minute of stand up material, then the crowd heckles and roasts them until they run out of insults.

stories.title: The 'Zipper Queen' volunteers at repair cafes to restore busted zippers
stories.summary: Michelle Elise is known in repair cafe circles as the "Zipper Queen." She finds that most broken zippers just need some TLC, not replacing.
